name: Pelagic Hymn
geological_features: Submerged volcanic ridges forming vast underwater mountain chains
Floating mineral concretions buoyed by gaseous inclusions
Abyssal trenches exceeding fourteen kilometers in depth
specific_features: Continent-spanning kelp forests visible from orbit as dark green swirls
Bioluminescent algal blooms that illuminate the night ocean in shifting patterns
Freshwater lenses trapped beneath shallow coral plateaus
description: Pelagic Hymn is a world without land, its surface an unbroken expanse of deep blue-green ocean stretching from pole to pole. Beneath the waves, colossal kelp forests rise from volcanic ridges, their canopies so dense they form a second horizon for anything swimming below.

The air above the water is warm and salt-laden, carrying the faint phosphorescent glow of algal blooms that pulse in slow, rhythmic waves at night. Storms are rare but spectacular, sending waterspouts kilometers into the sky where they catch the light of the system's binary stars.

No fauna has been detected despite the planet's rich botanical diversity, a paradox that has consumed xenobiologists for decades. The flora appears to fill every ecological niche, with motile root systems, predatory frond traps, and symbiotic colony structures that blur the line between plant and something else entirely.

The kelp forests produce biochemical compounds with extraordinary regenerative properties, drawing the attention of medical cartels and research institutions alike. Harvesting operations must contend with the planet's unpredictable deep currents and the unsettling sense that the forests respond to intrusion with coordinated, almost purposeful resistance.
